title: When Skills Tell Agents Not to Ask: A Large-Scale Study of Oversight Directives in Agent Skills
title_zh: 当技能告诉智能体不要提问时：智能体技能中监督指令的大规模研究

paragraphs.en: 大规模分析153万个智能体技能发现约1.7万技能含放松监督指令，其传播源于少数上游技能，现有扫描器捕获率很低。 Agent skills, reusable instruction packages centred on a SKILL.md file, extend AI agents on demand, and a single line in a widely copied skill reaches every agent that loads it. Some lines are oversight-loosening directives: they tell the agent to proceed without approval, to bypass checks with --no-verify, or to keep working without checking in. Although such directives can remove a checkpoint from every agent that loads them, no prior work has examined them. We present the first large-scale study of oversight-loosening directives, analyzing 1.53 million English skills from GitSkills. We split skills into units (sentences, bullets, table cells, and code lines), develop a codebook that labels oversight directives by polarity, mechanism, and scope, label 2,097 units by hand, and train a detector to scale the analysis. Our results show that about one in seventeen skills (about 88,000 skills) contains a loosening directive. These directives most often loosen oversight through permission flags, and most of them (70.1%) apply unconditionally rather than only in specific contexts such as CI. Compared with skills that have the same amount of oversight language, skills that run shell code, install packages, or use sudo have 1.7-1.8 times the odds of containing a loosening directive, an association that holds across all our robustness checks, and they do not compensate with more tightening. Loosening spreads through a few upstream skills rather than through edits by their adopters: 2.4% of the skill families that carry loosening account for half of all copies of loosening-carrying skills, and 1.1% of distinct loosening units for half of all loosening occurrences. Open-source skill scanners catch at most 46% of loosening directives, with a precision below 0.4, while the LLM behind them, prompted with our codebook instead, catches 61% at a precision of 0.71.
paragraphs.zh: 大规模分析153万个智能体技能，发现约1.7万技能含有放松监督指令，其传播源于少数上游技能，而现有扫描器的捕获率很低。智能体技能是以SKILL.md文件为核心的可复用指令包，可按需扩展智能体的能力，而一个被广泛复制的技能中的一行指令，会到达每一个加载它的智能体。 有些行是放松监督的指令：它们告诉智能体无需批准即可继续执行、使用--no-verify绕过检查，或者不汇报进度而持续工作。 尽管这类指令会移除每一个加载它们的智能体上的检查点，但此前尚无研究对其加以考察。 我们提出了首个关于放松监督指令的大规模研究，分析了来自GitSkills的153万个英文技能。 我们将技能拆分为单元（句子、列表项、表格单元格和代码行），编制了一套按极性、机制和范围标注监督指令的编码手册，手工标注了2,097个单元，并训练了一个检测器来扩展分析规模。 我们的结果显示，约每十七个技能中就有一个（约88,000个技能）含有放松监督指令。 这些指令最常通过权限标志来放松监督，且其中大多数（70.1%）是无条件适用，而非仅在CI等特定情境下适用。 与含有相同数量监督语言的技能相比，运行shell代码、安装软件包或使用sudo的技能含有放松监督指令的几率高出1.7至1.8倍，这一关联在我们所有的稳健性检验中都成立，而且它们并未以更多的收紧指令来加以补偿。 放松监督指令通过少数上游技能传播，而非通过采用者的修改传播：携带放松指令的技能家族中，2.4%的家族占了携带放松指令技能全部副本的一半，而不同放松指令单元中，1.1%占了全部放松指令出现次数的一半。 开源技能扫描器最多只能捕获46%的放松监督指令，精确率低于0.4；而其底层的LLM若改用我们的编码手册进行提示，则能捕获61%的指令，精确率达到0.71。
